title: LangKraft content records
description: Two record types. `entry` is a single item. `exchange` is a two-sided sequence, because half of every real conversation is what the other person says. Storage format is JSONL, one record per line.

claim.description: A factual claim with its provenance. A bare value without a source is a lint failure — this is the gate that makes 'I could not find a figure' distinguishable from 'I invented a figure'.

source.description: URL, or 'internal' for design reasoning. Must not be absent.

verified.description: true only if a critic agent fetched `source` and confirmed it says this. false is honest and permitted. ABSENT is a failure.

provenance.description: Where one content item came from. `class` is linted against the tier policy: Tier 0 accepts `authored` or `curated`, never `corpus`.

id.description: Source id from the spec's resources block.

external_id.description: Row id in the upstream source, e.g. a Tatoeba sentence id. Makes the item traceable back.

speaker.description: Only these two. A learner is one person in a conversation; everything else is noise.

direction.description: Inherited from the referenced entry, repeated here so an exchange can be read without a join.

entry_id.description: Null when this turn has no standalone entry — which is the normal case for the `them` side.

optional.description: True when a turn can be skipped without breaking the exchange. Real interactions have these and omitting them teaches the learner to stall.

id.description: Stable and never reused. Content is corrected by revision, not replacement, so a learner's history survives a spec change.

domain.description: 1 greetings/courtesy, 2 numbers/time, 3 money, 4 food, 5 accommodation, 6 transport, 7 directions, 8 shopping, 9 health, 10 emergencies, 11 people, 12 repair/survival

text_romanized.description: Null for Latin-script languages. Never a duplicate of text_native.

text_english.description: Null only when the spec sets language.gloss_mode: same_as_native, i.e. the calibration language whose gloss IS its native text.

register.description: neutral, or a language-specific level where the spec's register.system demands one.

direction.description: The receptive/productive split. A learner is spoken to faster than he speaks, so most items are `understand`.

why.description: One line. Why this item is in the floor. Lets him pick three on a tired day.

caution.description: What not to say, or where this fails. Optional but strongly preferred.

failure_flags.description: Written by the pipeline from the app's 'this failed me' flag. Never edited by hand.

exchange.description: A two-sided sequence. `scenario` names a situation, not a topic: 'checking into a room', not 'accommodation'. Topics are what a syllabus uses; situations are what a traveller meets.

order.description: Explicit display order, curated by usefulness. NOT alphabetical — alphabetical is arbitrary, and a first-time reader needs the exchanges that happen most often first.

turns.description: Minimum two: an exchange with one turn is a phrase.

tone_variant.description: One tone of one syllable. Variants within a tone_set differ ONLY by tone — that is the entire pedagogical point.

tone_name.description: mid, low, falling, high, rising (Thai); flat, rising, dipping, falling (Mandarin)

text_native.description: The syllable WITH its tone mark. The mark is the difference.

text_romanized.description: null for Latin; for a tonal language this carries an explicit tone number, e.g. maa3

text_english.description: What this tone MEANS. Without it a tone set teaches no contrast, only a squiggle.

text_note.description: Where the tone is drawn — above, below, on the vowel, after the syllable.

tone_set.description: A minimal contrast set: one syllable written several ways, differing only by tone. This is the visual half of a language the app cannot teach auditorily, and it is the only tone content a no-audio app can honestly ship.

syllable.description: The neutral bare syllable, if one exists.

variants.description: Minimum two. A single variant is not a contrast.
